page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The instance provides 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. System memory totals 192.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:2 compute-oriented ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU core. The hardware configuration contains zero integrated GPUs, dedicating its silicon footprint exclusively to CPU execution.

Storage and networking configurations follow a decoupled infrastructure design. The instance includes no local storage disks, necessitating the use of remote network storage volumes for OS boot drives and file data persistence. Baseline network throughput is rated at 32 Gbps, supporting high-throughput inter-node traffic, while complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

The hardware configuration trades high per-core RAM density and local NVMe scratch space for concentrated multi-core CPU capacity. This yields high cost efficiency for compute-dense workloads that do not require expansive memory footprints or accelerated graphics processing. Best-fit use cases include distributed compilation, high-throughput web serving, video transcoding, and large-scale batch processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8a.24xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by 96 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9T24 processor operating at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with a 1:2 compute profile, it includes 192.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core) alongside a 32 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system contains no integrated GPU accelerators and features no onboard local storage, relying on network-attached storage for persistent storage operations. This hardware layout maximizes CPU core density while avoiding the cost overhead of surplus memory or dedicated accelerators. As a result, it provides strong qualitative efficiency for compute-bound applications, including multi-threaded software compilation, batch analytics, computational modeling, and dense containerized web workloads.
